findings.claim: §12.7.13 states the TOCTOU window is 'closed by GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04's RUNNER_TEMP being a runner-private directory (mode 0700, owned by the runner user).' The specific assertion 'mode 0700' is not documented in GitHub's official runner specification and is likely inaccurate. GitHub's runner creates RUNNER_TEMP via CreateDirectory() with the process umask applied (typically yielding 0755 on Linux, not 0700). The practical security conclusion is sound — the ephemeral single-user VM prevents TOCTOU exploitation regardless of exact directory mode, since TOCTOU write-protection derives from file ownership (runner:runner) not directory stickiness — but the specific technical claim made as the justification for 'closed' is unverified and likely wrong.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 line 1039: 'There is a TOCTOU window between the verify and the cp — closed by GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04's RUNNER_TEMP being a runner-private directory (mode 0700, owned by the runner user).' GitHub public documentation for ubuntu-24.04 hosted runners does not specify RUNNER_TEMP directory mode. GitHub's open-source runner creates the temp directory with CreateDirectory() (no explicit chmod). On Linux with a standard umask of 022, the resulting mode is 0755. R1 SAFE-004 original evidence acknowledged the ubuntu-24.04 RUNNER_TEMP is 'runner-private' but did not cite the 0700 mode as a formally documented property.
findings.impact: Negligible security impact — on hosted runners the VM is isolated with a single runner user, so TOCTOU is not exploitable regardless of whether RUNNER_TEMP is 0700 or 0755. Self-hosted runner operators reading §12.7.13 may incorrectly infer that setting RUNNER_TEMP to 0700 matches GitHub's practice when the actual protection is the ownership model. If a self-hosted operator sets RUNNER_TEMP to 0755 thinking it diverges from GitHub's documented behavior, they may worry unnecessarily. Conversely, the caveat 'On self-hosted runners, ensure RUNNER_TEMP is not group/world-writable' correctly identifies what actually matters (write access), which makes this a documentation-precision nit rather than a security gap.
findings.mitigation: Change §12.7.13 line 1039 to: 'closed by the runner user being the exclusive writer on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 (RUNNER_TEMP is owned by the runner user; the ephemeral single-user VM has no other local accounts that could exploit the window).' Remove the 'mode 0700' parenthetical — the mode is not formally documented by GitHub and the protection derives from ownership, not directory stickiness. Retain the self-hosted caveat 'On self-hosted runners, ensure RUNNER_TEMP is not group/world-writable.'

findings.claim: assert_bare_binary_shape() uses '|| true' at the magic-byte extraction: magic="$(head -c 2 "${path}" 2>/dev/null | xxd -p 2>/dev/null || true)". If xxd is absent from the runner image, or if head or xxd fails for any reason other than a permission error, magic is silently set to empty string and the check [ "${magic}" = "1f8b" ] evaluates false — the shape guard is silently voided without any diagnostic. The failure mode is not a security bypass (cp and the regal version smoke test are fail-closed downstream), but the defensive shape check can be made a no-op by the absence of xxd without any warning.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 249–256: assert_bare_binary_shape() body — 'magic="$(head -c 2 "${path}" 2>/dev/null | xxd -p 2>/dev/null || true)"' followed by '[ "${magic}" = "1f8b" ]'. The ubuntu-24.04 runner image includes xxd (part of vim-common), but xxd availability is not checked or asserted. If xxd is missing, magic="" and the gzip-detection branch is never entered. The downstream resolve_regal() caller does 'cp "${REGAL_SOURCE}" "${BIN_DIR}/regal"' and '"${BIN_DIR}/regal" version >/dev/null || emit_infra_failure' — the smoke test catches a gzip-shaped binary (binary format error), but with the opaque message SAFE-003 was specifically written to replace.
findings.impact: If xxd is absent, assert_bare_binary_shape silently becomes a no-op: a tarball-shaped Regal binary passes the shape check with empty magic, and the downstream regal version smoke test catches it with 'Regal runtime failed its post-download smoke test' — the same opaque message SAFE-003 was designed to replace. In this scenario, SAFE-003's closure regresses: the diagnostic improvement disappears without any signal to the operator. Not a security bypass (still fail-closed), but a silent degradation of the defensive diagnostic.
findings.mitigation: Replace '|| true' with explicit xxd-availability check: before 'magic=$(head -c 2 ...)', add 'if ! command -v xxd >/dev/null 2>&1; then emit_infra_failure "xxd not found on runner; cannot assert Regal asset shape"; fi'. Alternatively, replace 'xxd -p' with a portable Python one-liner to avoid the xxd dependency: 'magic="$(python3 -c "import sys; d=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read(2); print(d.hex())" "${path}" 2>/dev/null || true)"' — python3 is already required by the workflow (multiple earlier steps). Either change makes the shape check self-consistent with the fail-closed principle.

findings.claim: §12.7.13 fork-operator guidance cross-references §12.7.4 / §12.7.1 for CODEOWNERS recommendations on lockfile protection in SCP forks, but those sections cover the adopter's caller-wrapper CODEOWNERS (protecting .github/workflows/policy-check.yml in the adopter's repo), not scripts/scp-policy-check.lock or scripts/.tool-versions CODEOWNERS in a fork of the SCP repo itself. A fork operator following the reference would find guidance on protecting their caller wrapper but no concrete guidance on protecting their fork's lockfile.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 line 1037: 'Adopters who run their own SCP fork should mirror this CODEOWNERS coverage on their lockfile — see §12.7.4 / §12.7.1 wrapper CODEOWNERS recommendations.' §12.7.1 line 796: 'CODEOWNERS for the wrapper. Multi-maintainer adopters MUST protect this file with CODEOWNERS so a single PR cannot silently delete the fork-PR if:, weaken permissions:, or change the pinned SHA without an owning reviewer.' This covers the adopter's wrapper file, not the SCP lockfile in a fork. §12.7.4 (from context, the scp/rule-config.yaml CODEOWNERS section, referenced at line 1048: 'see §11.10 ... referenced from §12.7.4') also covers adopter config-file CODEOWNERS, not fork lockfile CODEOWNERS.
findings.impact: Fork operators who run their own SCP fork and follow the §12.7.13 guidance + cross-reference will protect their caller wrapper (§12.7.1 outcome) but may not add 'scripts/** @<owner>' to their fork's CODEOWNERS, leaving their lockfile unprotected. The SCP repo itself has the correct CODEOWNERS coverage; the risk is to derivative forks that read this guidance and follow the cross-reference. Low probability — very few forks expected — but directly relevant to the SAFE-002 closure's stated intent of documenting the governance model for fork operators.
findings.mitigation: Replace '— see §12.7.4 / §12.7.1 wrapper CODEOWNERS recommendations' with a self-contained inline instruction: 'In your fork's CODEOWNERS, add "scripts/** @<owner>" and "vendor/** @<owner>" inserted before any CODEOWNERS self-protection line (last-match-wins ordering — see the SCP repo's CODEOWNERS comment block for the ORDERING INVARIANT). This is analogous to the pattern documented for the caller wrapper in §12.7.1.'

structured_review.summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS — all five R1 safety findings are genuinely closed; fixpoint criterion met (zero new CRIT or MAJ). R2 yields four nit-severity findings only. SAFE-001 closure verified: §12.7.13 accurately states Regal is pinned in scripts/.tool-versions (regal 0.40.0) and SHA256-verified per platform — lockfile has all four platform entries (linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-arm64, darwin-x64), workflow reads REGAL_VERSION via read_tool_version and REGAL_SHA256 via read_lockfile_field, resolve_regal() calls verify_sha256 before returning the path, and TF-020H3-001 is correctly marked closed. SAFE-002 closure verified: CODEOWNERS now contains 'scripts/** @jrnb2024' and 'vendor/** @jrnb2024' inserted at lines 55–56, before the '/CODEOWNERS @jrnb2024' self-protection at line 68 — last-match-wins ordering invariant holds; scripts/** does not over-cover (sanitize_review_finding.py and generate_demo_deck.py are governance-tooling and correctly route to @jrnb2024); no existing rule was superseded by the new wildcard (all prior rules cover disjoint paths). SAFE-003 closure verified: assert_bare_binary_shape() is present and called after BOTH the curl-download path AND the vendor-fallback path in resolve_regal() — the gzip magic-byte check (1f8b) emits an explicit emit_infra_failure message with the correct remediation guidance. SAFE-004 closure verified: §12.7.13 documents the RUNNER_TEMP TOCTOU assumption with the self-hosted-runner caveat. SAFE-005 closure verified: policy-check.yml lines 165–171 now catch (KeyError, TypeError) in read_lockfile_field. SAFE-003 adversarial analysis (instruction §3a): a SHA256-verified gzip-shaped binary cannot trick the shape check — if the lockfile pins a gzip binary, the lockfile itself would need to be compromised first, which requires CODEOWNERS approval. The assert_bare_binary_shape defensive check is specifically for the future case where the lockfile is legitimately updated to a tarball-shaped Regal but resolve_regal() is not updated in lockstep — sound design. New nit findings: R2-SAFE-001 (DISPATCH-NOTE Files section not updated with ADOPT-001, CODEOWNERS, FIX-ROUND-1.md after fix-round-1 — audit-scope gap, not a bypass); R2-SAFE-002 (§12.7.13 'mode 0700' RUNNER_TEMP claim unverified against GitHub runner specification — likely 0755 in practice, security conclusion remains sound); R2-SAFE-003 (assert_bare_binary_shape's '|| true' silently voids shape check if xxd absent — fail-closed downstream but defeats the SAFE-003 diagnostic improvement); R2-SAFE-004 (§12.7.13 fork-operator lockfile CODEOWNERS guidance cross-references §12.7.1/§12.7.4 which cover wrapper CODEOWNERS, not lockfile CODEOWNERS — misdirected reference for fork operators).
